items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: when Bobby Hackett played with Glenn Miller, Glenn Miller had him, Bobby didn’t have to carry it

ctx.x: So the idea of amplification for the guitar, I know Freddie Green was never really amplified right? He just kind of would basically feel that sound.

Not that I know of. He once went out and they got him a mic and an amp or something, but it was never used, and later on I heard that you know when Bobby Hackett played with Glenn Miller, Glenn Miller had him, Bobby didn’t have to carry it, the band boy had to carry an amp all over the place, but Bobby never used it, he didn’t like it. And no, of course we heard Oscar Moore, that was a hot ticket then, the King Cole Trio was the hot ticket, and we all had those, you know all the kids had those records and we’d…

jogging or lifting weights or something like similar to that, you know, you have to use a higher action and heavier gauge strings. But once you get it going, you know, he said, “It’s a wonderful feeling. I was with the bass and the drums and we were all tight, together and we got a blend” and stuff like that. So but getting back to your question, so that’s what I really wanted to do. And it was, if I did take some crappy solos once in a while, that came later. That came because as the music business got worse and…
